specDepartures.spec: Require a generated name, 'so every name a submitter can take is one the API server handed it'. Line 3: a submitter can no longer create a Service under a name the API server did not hand it.
specDepartures.plan: A validating policy alone cannot do this. The recommended (a2) adds a mutating policy that removes a submitter's own name when generateName is set, a validating rule for generateName and the generator's shape, and a five-character-tail rule on Services. The guarantee then holds for every Job and every standing Service, but not for a forged-owner Service of generator shape during its garbage-collection window. Only option (b) meets line 3 literally.
specDepartures.evidence: Measured on a local kube-apiserver v1.36.2: a validating policy sees {name: X, generateName: x} exactly as given, and a generated name looks the same as a client-chosen one of matching shape. A mutating policy in front replaced the client's name in every case. The live cluster serves MutatingAdmissionPolicy v1.

summary: The fix requires a server-generated Job name through a mutating and validating policy pair, not a validating rule alone.
acceptance: Line 3, as the architect rewrites it: every Job and every standing Service carries a server-handed name, and a forged-owner Service is bounded by the garbage collector's sweep. Option (b) was refused.
